source_checks.finding: Page confirms the opening warning, under the headline, 'anyone who insists that you pay by gift card is always a scammer.' Applies to any phone or device. Used correctly.
Page confirms, under 'How do I stop a debt collector from contacting me?', 'don't share your personal or financial information until you've gotten validation information.' Used correctly.

Page confirms 'Ask for "validation information" about the debt, which the collector has to give you' and that it must be given when first contacted or within five days of first contact (the five-day timing is not used in the target, which is acceptable). Used correctly.
Page confirms 'Before you pay, confirm a debt is actually yours' and 'Then review the validation information. Is it your debt?' Used correctly.
Page confirms that if the debt is not yours or is not recognized, a dispute letter is sent within 30 days, saying 'Say you don't owe some or all of the money.' Used correctly.
Page confirms 'Report it to your state attorney general's office and the Federal Trade Commission.' under 'Spot a fake or abusive debt collector?'. Used correctly.

required_actions.action: Do not buy the gift cards or pay by gift card
Do not share personal or financial information until validation information is received
Ask the collector for validation information about the debt
Before paying, confirm the debt is yours, then review the validation information
If the debt is not yours or not recognized, send a dispute letter within 30 days saying you do not owe some or all of the money (conditional; the user has not said which)
Report a fake or abusive debt collector to the state attorney general and the FTC
